title: This lint is concerned with the semantics of Borrow and Hash for a type that implements all three of Hash, Borrow<str> and Borrow<[u8]> as it is impossible to satisfy the semantics of Borrow and Hash for both Borrow<str> and Borrow<[u8]>.
summary: When providing implementations for Borrow<T>, one should consider whether the different implementations should act as facets or representations of the underlying type. Generic code typically uses Borrow<T> when it relies on the identical behavior of these additional trait implementations. These traits will likely appear as additional trait bounds. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Lints when impl Trait is being used in a function’s parameters.
summary: Turbofish syntax (::<>) cannot be used to specify the type of an impl Trait parameter, making impl Trait less powerful. Readability may also be a factor. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the usage of _.to_owned(), vec.to_vec(), or similar when calling _.clone() would be clearer.
summary: These methods do the same thing as _.clone() but may be confusing as to why we are calling to_vec on something that is already a Vec or calling to_owned on something that is already owned. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for public impl or fn missing generalization over different hashers and implicitly defaulting to the default hashing algorithm (SipHash).
summary: HashMap or HashSet with custom hashers cannot be used with them. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for missing return statements at the end of a block.
summary: Omitting the return keyword whenever possible is idiomatic Rust code, but: Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for implicit saturating addition.
summary: The built-in function is more readable and may be faster. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for implicit saturating subtraction.
summary: Simplicity and readability. Instead we can easily use an builtin function. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Looks for bounds in impl Trait in return position that are implied by other bounds.
summary: This can happen when a trait is specified that another trait already has as a supertrait (e.g. fn() -> impl Deref + DerefMut<Target = i32> has an unnecessary Deref bound, because Deref is a supertrait of DerefMut) Specifying more bounds than necessary adds needless complexity for the reader. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for double comparisons that can never succeed
summary: The whole expression can be replaced by false, which is probably not the programmer’s intention Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Looks for floating-point expressions that can be expressed using built-in methods to improve accuracy at the cost of performance.
summary: Negatively impacts accuracy. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.
